The bed from which this small cone rises is solidified lava that has been thrown up during past eruptions of Vesuvius and settled in the vent. In this way the vent is closed and the floor rises each year nearer to the top. Small inner craters, as the one shown, allow for the escape of the gasses and vapors generated below, but as the rock hardens and time passes, still greater energy is being stored, which, when its strength is great enough will blast a way through the accumulated debris, resulting in another serious eruption.
